pointers.sentence: Text helpers: `Truncator` and `django/utils/text.py`

`django/utils/text.py` holds the text helpers that Django's filters, models, forms, storage and middleware share: `Truncator`, which cuts text to a number of characters or words, plain or as HTML; `slugify` (`django/utils/text.py:slugify`), `get_valid_filename`, `capfirst` and `get_text_list`; the splitting of a template tag's arguments; and the gzip compression of `GZipMiddleware`.

`django/utils/text.py` holds the text helpers that Django's filters, models, forms, storage and middleware share: `Truncator`, which cuts text to a number of characters or words, plain or as HTML; `slugify` (`django/utils/text.py:slugify`), `get_valid_filename`, `capfirst` and `get_text_list`; the splitting of a template tag's arguments; and the gzip compression of `GZipMiddleware`.
Beside it, `django/utils/xmlutils.py` has `SimplerXMLGenerator`, the serializer's and the feeds' XML writer.

`capfirst`, `wrap`, `get_valid_filename`, `get_text_list`, `normalize_newlines`, `phone2numeric`, `unescape_string_literal` and `slugify` are decorated with `keep_lazy_text`: with plain arguments the function runs at once; given a `Promise` among them, it returns a lazy value that runs the function each time it is used (`django/utils/functional.py:keep_lazy`).
So a form field's label, made by `capfirst` from a model field's lazily translated verbose name, is translated when shown (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.formfield`).
`Truncator` is a `SimpleLazyObject` whose function makes the text a string: making one does nothing with the text (`django/utils/text.py:Truncator`).

The four truncating filters make one for each value ([The built-in filters](../templates/filters.md)) (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:truncatechars`), as do the admin's raw-id widget and `migrate --plan` (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.describe_operation`).

The four truncating filters make one for each value ([The built-in filters](../templates/filters.md)) (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:truncatechars`), as do the admin's raw-id widget and `migrate --plan` (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.describe_operation`).

One given that holds "%(truncated_text)s" is used as a format in the same way; any other is appended to the cut text, unless that text already ends with it (`django/utils/text.py:add_truncation_text`).

`calculate_truncate_chars_length` subtracts the truncation text's own characters from the length asked for, so a cut result, mark included, is that long unless the mark alone is longer (`django/utils/text.py:Truncator._text_chars`).
`words` splits at white space and joins the words it keeps with single spaces, so it loses the text's line breaks even when nothing is cut (`django/utils/text.py:Truncator._text_words`).

With `html=True` the text is fed to an `html.parser.HTMLParser`, a `TruncateCharsHTMLParser` or a `TruncateWordsHTMLParser`, and only the text between tags is counted (`django/utils/text.py:TruncateHTMLParser`).
A start tag is copied as written and, unless it is a void element such as `"br"` (`django/utils/html.py:VOID_ELEMENTS`), pushed on a stack of open tags.

When the count runs out inside a run of text, the parser writes the part that fits and the truncation text, stops, and closes every tag still open, the latest first (`django/utils/text.py:TruncateHTMLParser.feed`).
And the words' parser counts the pieces of each run of text, so white space standing alone between two tags is a word (`django/utils/text.py:TruncateWordsHTMLParser.process`):
`slugify` makes a slug, lower-case words joined by hyphens for a URL (`django/utils/text.py:slugify`).
Within Django only the template filter of the same name calls it (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:slugify`).
A result that is empty, `"."` or `".."` raises `SuspiciousFileOperation` (`django/utils/text.py:get_valid_filename`).
`capfirst` returns a false value as it is, makes anything else a string, and upper-cases its first character (`django/utils/text.py:capfirst`).

Django calls it mostly on verbose names: `Field.formfield` makes a form field's label with it, `Model.unique_error_message` and `Model.date_error_message` the names in their messages (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.formfield`, `django/db/models/base.py:Model.unique_error_message`), and the admin and the authentication app their labels, titles and prompts.

The template filter `capfirst` is a function of its own (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:capfirst`).
The separator is translated with `gettext` and the last word defaults to a lazy translation of "or", so both are in the language active when the function runs (`django/utils/text.py:get_text_list`).
`Model.unique_error_message` names the fields of a unique set with it, and the template parser the end tags it expected (`django/template/base.py:Parser.invalid_block_tag`).

`smart_split` splits text at white space but keeps a quoted phrase whole, quotes and escapes included, and `unescape_string_literal` takes the quotes off such a phrase, raising `ValueError` for text that is not one (`django/utils/text.py:smart_split`).

`Token.split_contents` splits a template tag's contents with the first, and a template variable that is a quoted literal is read with the second (`django/template/base.py:Token.split_contents`; [From text to nodes: the lexer and the parser](../templates/compiling.md)); the admin splits a search term with both, keeping a quoted phrase one term (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_search_results`).

`Token.split_contents` splits a template tag's contents with the first, and a template variable that is a quoted literal is read with the second (`django/template/base.py:Token.split_contents`; [From text to nodes: the lexer and the parser](../templates/compiling.md)); the admin splits a search term with both, keeping a quoted phrase one term (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_search_results`).

`wrap` wraps text to a width with `textwrap.TextWrapper`, keeping the line breaks already there and never breaking a long word, so a line can be longer than the width; it is the `wordwrap` filter's (`django/utils/text.py:wrap`).
And `django/utils/lorem_ipsum.py` makes the placeholder Latin of `{% lorem %}` ([The built-in tags](../templates/tags.md)).

`compress_string` compresses bytes with gzip, and `compress_sequence` and `acompress_sequence` an iterator and an asynchronous iterator, yielding the header first and then what each item adds (`django/utils/text.py:compress_sequence`).

Given `max_random_bytes`, they write a file name in the header, a run of the byte "a" of a random length below that number, so the compressed length varies; without it, the same bytes, or the same items, always compress to the same output, since all three write 0 as the header's time (`django/utils/text.py:compress_string`).
`GZipMiddleware` passes its `GZipMiddleware.max_random_bytes`, 100 (`django/middleware/gzip.py:GZipMiddleware.process_response`).

The documentation's reason: compression may expose a site to attacks such as BREACH, and adding a random number of bytes to each response, a technique called Heal The Breach, makes them less effective (`docs/ref/middleware.txt`, `docs/releases/4.2.txt`).

`SimplerXMLGenerator` is the standard library's `xml.sax.saxutils.XMLGenerator` with a shortcut, `SimplerXMLGenerator.addQuickElement`, for an element with text and no children (`django/utils/xmlutils.py:SimplerXMLGenerator`).
